For publication-grade pipelines, `tidytmle` accepts custom `recipes`, `parsnip` model specifications, `workflows`, and `workflowsets::workflow_set` ensembles directly—while enforcing causal guardrails automatically.

## Role-Aware Recipe Splitting & `workflow_set` Super Learning

A common source of subtle bugs in manual causal ML pipelines is accidentally leaking the treatment column $A$ or cluster ID into the propensity model $g(W)$ when reusing a single `recipe(y ~ ., data = df)`. `tidytmle` automatically clones and adapts the preprocessing recipe per nuisance factor (`Q`, `g`, and `C`), guaranteeing that $A$ is retained in $Q(A, W)$ and $C(A, W)$ while strictly excluded from $g$'s predictors:

```{r level2, message = FALSE}
library(tidytmle)
library(recipes)
library(parsnip)
library(workflowsets)

df <- sim_causal_cohort(
  n = 350,
  outcome_type = "continuous",
  censoring_rate = 0.15,
  n_clusters = 15L,
  seed = 101
)

base_rec <- recipe(y ~ ., data = df) |>
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors())

q_wf_set <- workflow_set(
  preproc = list(base = base_rec),
  models = list(
    glm = linear_reg() |> set_engine("glm"),
    enet = linear_reg(penalty = 0.05, mixture = 0.5) |> set_engine("glmnet")
  )
)

g_spec <- logistic_reg() |> set_engine("glm")

fit_l2 <- tmle_spec(
  outcome    = y,
  treatment  = a,
  covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),
  censoring  = delta,
  id         = clinic_id,
  estimand   = "ate"
) |>
  set_preprocessing(base_rec) |>
  set_outcome_learners(q_wf_set) |>
  set_treatment_learners(g_spec) |>
  set_resamples(v_folds = 5L) |>
  fit(data = df)

fit_l2
```

## Automatic Informative-Missingness Handling & Case Weights

When `outcome` contains missing values (`NA`) and `censoring` is omitted, `tidytmle` automatically creates an observation indicator $\Delta = \mathbb{I}(\neg\text{is.na}(Y))$ and models informative missingness $C(A, W) = P(\Delta = 1 \mid A, W)$ rather than silently dropping incomplete rows. Native `hardhat::importance_weights()` and `hardhat::frequency_weights()` are likewise propagated through both nuisance workflows and the cluster-robust EIF variance estimator:

```{r missingness, fig.alt = "Weighted covariate balance Love plot comparing unadjusted vs TMLE/IPW standardized mean differences"}
df_miss <- dplyr::select(df, -delta)
df_miss$survey_wt <- hardhat::importance_weights(runif(nrow(df_miss), 0.7, 1.5))

fit_auto_c <- tmle_spec(
  outcome    = y,
  treatment  = a,
  covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),
  id         = clinic_id,
  weights    = survey_wt
) |>
  set_resamples(v_folds = 5L) |>
  fit(data = df_miss)

glance(fit_auto_c)
autoplot(fit_auto_c, type = "balance")
```
